# Mike Basios — full profile

Optimisation systems that improve code, models and agents under measurement · Co-founder & CTO, [TurinTech AI](https://turintech.ai) · London. Canonical page: https://mike-turintech.github.io/ (short version: https://mike-turintech.github.io/llms.txt)

## About

I build optimisation systems that improve code, models and agents under measurement, and I have done it in production for nine years. I am the co-founder and CTO of [TurinTech AI](https://turintech.ai), a UCL spinout, and the builder of [Artemis](https://www.turintech.ai/product/overview) and its Discovery engine: an optimisation platform that combines evolutionary search with multi-LLM orchestration to explore hundreds of candidate changes to code, models and agents, benchmarks every one on the real workload, and ships only measured winners as pull requests — on any metric a team cares about, from throughput and memory to accuracy and cost. The guiding idea: if it can be measured, it can be optimised. Optimisations Artemis found have been merged upstream by the maintainers of NVIDIA TensorRT-LLM, llama.cpp and OpenAI Whisper, among others; the diffs and benchmarks are on [turintech.ai/open-source](https://www.turintech.ai/open-source). Before that I worked on data and software systems in investment banking.

My own part, kept short because the team reads this too: the original research and paper on Darwinian data-structure selection, and the first Artemis — the name comes from my thesis, where it was the cloud-based, multi-objective optimiser that rewrote the data structures of 44 programs — then the design of the system as it is today, and the first version of Discovery. On the papers since, my role has been the research hypothesis and the design of the experiments; the team does the rest, and the team is the point.

What excites me most is autoresearch: recursive, self-learning systems that form hypotheses about a codebase or model, run the experiments, keep what measurably works and feed the result back into their own search. Discovery is the first production version of that loop, and the research on evolving LLM-based agents is where it goes next: a meta system — one that improves the systems that improve the code.

I studied informatics at the University of Piraeus (BSc, first class) and computer science at the University of Edinburgh (MSc with distinction), started my research there with Stratis Viglas, and moved my PhD to University College London, where Earl Barr supervised it with Ilya Sergey. [The thesis](https://discovery.ucl.ac.uk/10070648/), on Darwinian code optimisation — evolving programs under measurement to select data structures and code — was published at ESEC/FSE, ICSE, ASE and SSBSE and recognised with an ACM GECCO [Human-Competitive Results (Humies)](https://www.human-competitive.org/) award.

Research and teaching have run alongside the company from the start. At Edinburgh I taught in the lab for the Extreme Computing course, my first hands-on work with Hadoop, Spark and the wider big-data stack; at UCL I supervised MSc theses and projects, many run as internships with banks and technology companies. Since founding TurinTech I have co-supervised PhD students working on the problems behind our products — several have defended, others are in progress — and collaborated with senior researchers at UCL, Leeds (through an Innovate UK Knowledge Transfer Partnership), Surrey, King's College London and Warwick, with support from a Horizon 2020 grant. Most of my publications come out of that work. We started by optimising machine-learning models, with evoML, an evolutionary AutoML studio, and generalised what we learned into Artemis — so each research problem solved along the way, from data-structure selection to LLM-guided search and agent optimisation, has ended up in the product. Away from work I play 9-a-side football.

## Publications

Full record on [DBLP](https://dblp.org/pid/123/5293), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=8r8p0skAAAAJ) (1,100+ citations, h-index 10) and [Semantic Scholar](https://www.semanticscholar.org/author/Michail-Basios/2907390). Listed as Michail Basios in most venues. Selected: search-based and LLM-guided software optimisation, evolutionary computation and the research behind Artemis; a few finance side-projects are omitted.
